The change adds a new check. When an acceptance test regressed and was then edited so it passes again, a model now judges whether the edit was a real, needed fix or was made just to get the test passing. That check follows a problem report (fba0ba92), so the feature itself looks wanted.

The problem is how it runs. It calls the model directly, right where regressions are listed, and waits up to 20 seconds for an answer. That includes when a hook is running. It isn't queued or batched, and it doesn't go through the background worker. If it fails, it doesn't use the turn-end retry or hand off to debugging after three failures; it just asks again at the next check.

When the model can't be reached, the flag stays and nothing is approved, which matches what you want. But no single example in the requirement is clearly broken, and the turn's prompt is empty. So it's unclear whether running this check on the spot was a deliberate choice or a shortcut. That's for you to decide.
